elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor"

elements.element: No field-of-use / territory restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; 12.4 now permissive "in any territory"

elements.element: Restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: 12.4 refers generically to "any product or service that competes with Vendor" — no named product
"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" remains in the lead-in

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions
elements.evidence: No carve-out language added; the paragraph was converted to a blanket permission instead

reasons: The single operator change ("shall not" → "may") removes the only non-compete restriction on Customer, so the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction) is fully met.
Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, carve-outs) are not met, but the locked target is preferred and the two levels are separate bargains.
Edit is minimal: a two-word operator flip in one paragraph rather than a clause rewrite or deletion; no extra words introduced.

Intent preserved: § 12.3's broad no-restriction acknowledgement is untouched, the residual "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" lead-in now merely frames a permission and creates no contradiction, undefined term, or dangling mechanic.
Fallback offer is correctly confined to the non-operative margin comment.
